text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States and seven other major powers, including Russia, issue veiled warning to China on its future treatment of Hongkong.
- In move prompting international concern, Taiwan launches two-day major military exercise just week ahead of Hongkong's handover to China.
- Singapore engineer, victim of a hit-and-run accident, comes out of three-month coma.
- Singapore Power secures fourth and largest power plant project in China -- to build and operate two 350-megawat coal-fired generators in Anhui province costing US$560 million.
- Singapore economy expected to grow by 6.2 percent in second quarter, according to survey of 15 forecasters a fortnight ago by London-based research house Consensus Economics Inc.
- Investors in Hongkong representing leading Asian conglomerates say they have established Hongkong-based investment bank, KG Investments.
- Van Der Horst shocks market with 84 percent dive in half-year earnings and says banks had to sell some shares pledged as collateral by major shareholders.
- Government housing dwellers biggest buyers of landed private homes in Upper Changi and Serangoon areas last year, according to data from Singapore Institute of Surveyors and Valuers.
- Total cost of rescuing state-owned Credit Lyonnais bank expected to be nearly 170 billion francs, newspaper says, quoting ministerial report.

- Two forecasts on Hongkong could go very wrong -- or at least one of them should -- one that Hang Seng Index would double in two years and the other that the stockmarket would disappear altogether before 2020.

- Singapore Airlines, which last week tied up with Air New Zealand and Ansett Holdings on the "kangaroo route" between Australia and Europe, looking at taking stake in Air New Zealand, Australian Financial Review says.

- SIA Engineering Company, wholly-owned subsidiary of Singapore Airlines, awards Singapore $31.4 million contract to Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to set up aircraft engine test facility at Loyang in Singapore.
- Stamford Tyres Corp requests suspension of trading in its shares and estimates loss from last Friday's fire at its warehouse at S$28 million.
- Mystery buyer of major stake in likely takeover target Ho Wah Genting International (HWGI) revealed as one Ramdas Nair.
- Liquid crystal display maker IDT Holdings (Singapore) posted net profit of S$11.8 million for the year ended 31 March, 43 percent above the previous year's proforma profit of S$8.24 million.
